newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russian MinFins pause after recent rise.
newsitem.headline: Russian MinFins pause after recent rise.

text.p: Prices of Russian MinFin bonds were little changed in calm range-trading on Tuesday as the market paused for breath after a week-long rise, but dealers said the upward trend was likely to resume.
"The market is rather quiet today and is locked up in a narrow range. It has achieved the levels for taking profits," one dealer said.
Dealers said bonds were traded today in the ranges of 78.25-78.75, 52.20-52.80, 34.20-34.70, 39.60-40.00 and 29.30-29.75 respectively.
They forecast prices were likely to rise further after some days of treading water.

"The market is fairly strong due to the fact that Vnesh debt prices rose... The trend is steady and what is also good for MinFins is the upward trend in the global emerging market," Eurobank dealer Olivier Coursault said.
Dealers noted that prices had risen over the last seven days on speculation rating agencies would award Russia an investment grade for its forthcoming Eurobond.
"Speculation about a possible investment-grade rating is no longer enough to push up prices. We will see what to do when it is finally announced," said one dealer.
Deputy Finance Minister Mikhail Kasyanov told Reuters on Friday there might be some news about Russia's investment rating later this week.
